newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares-bought the rumour, selling the fact.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares-bought the rumour, selling the fact.

text.p: Russia's Jekyll and Hyde shares market, known for its quick temper and quick gains, has turned a bit bearish despite recent good news, but stock analysts on Wednesday said the lull in the bull run was temporary.
"Whenever we have a bit of good news, the market corrects," said Gavin Rankin, director of research at Moscow's Troika-Dialog brokerage.
The market has failed to react in March to signs of economic recovery and the appointment of a strong reformist government with a mandate from President Boris Yeltsin to fix Russia fast.
"It implies the market has discounted the good news," Rankin said.
"The market is able to hold at the current levels, though there will probably be a period of wait and see -- we are not exactly seeing a rush of buyers," he predicted.
The Russian Trading System (RTS) 23-share index fell three percent on Wednesday to close at 320.23 after Tuesday's 330.01.
The index gained about 50 percent in the first two months of the year and is worth five times its value a year ago.

Analysts said leading shares could drift a couple of percent lower through the end of the month but added that the investable market had grown beyond the most liquid shares which saw the biggest capital inflows and price appreciation early this year.
Ten shares captured 78 percent of the dollar volume on the RTS in January.
"That trend is not as evident any more," said Tom Balestrery, director of research at Creditanstalt Investment Bank. "Liquidity is increasing in the second tier because prices are going up."
"The RTS index most accurately reflects the speculative mood of active traders, not necessarily a consensus of overall market participants."

CentreInvest research chief James Fenkner said investors were redeploying funds from fairly or over-valued shares to less known issues after rushing into the market in January and February, when they bought whatever was available.
"The tide which raised all boats was the first two months of the year," he said. "Now it's all about finding which boat is better and getting into it."
The weakness among leading shares over the last week has not been felt by second tiers, such as retailer GUM, which rose to $28.30 on Wednesday from $27.00 on Tuesday.
Fenkner said the manufacturing sector would see share prices rising as confidence in the economy grew.

Analysts said they doubted the market would see another feeding frenzy but predicted the tone would improve in April as Russia and the International Monetary Fund agreed an economic plan for the year.
They said the Russian pause had been partly influenced by expectations of an interest rate hike in the U.S., one of the first signs Russia is beginning to correlate with world markets.
But real investor confidence would gather as the new reform team led by First Deputy Premier Anatoly Chubais put together a plan and began to show movement, if not results, they said.
"Although you have proven individuals, their ability to work together as a team is still not proven," said Balestrery.
